What the app stores, and what it never does.
Works entirely on your phone. No account, no ads, and no internet permission at all.

CloudSaver is 100% offline - it does not even hold the INTERNET permission. Your photos, videos, names and locations never leave the phone. No analytics, no ads, no accounts. The app writes only to its own folders. Automatic safety snapshots are hidden files, so nothing shows up in your gallery or Files app unless you tap Export yourself. Originals are never deleted automatically. State snapshots contain only file names, dates, sizes and hashes - never your photos or thumbnails. One honest note: no Android app can be made impossible to decompile; CloudSaver protects you with least privilege and tamper evidence instead. Terms: the app is provided as is, without any warranty; keep checking your cloud backup yourself.

Everything happens on the phone. Video bitrate comes from output pixels × fps (H.264: 0.10 bits per pixel per frame, HEVC: 0.065). 1080p30 H.264 ≈ 6 Mbps. Photos are resized to the preset megapixel limit at JPEG quality 80-85.
H.264 plays on every device. HEVC is about 35% smaller at the same quality, but older devices may not support it. H.264 is the default.
EXIF, GPS and dates are always copied. Rotation is baked in upright. If a compressed file would be bigger, the original is copied as-is - an item is never lost.

It does four things, in order. It finds the photos and videos in your gallery, makes a smaller copy of each one, puts those copies in a folder called Pictures/CloudSaver, and then keeps track of which ones reached your cloud. It never uploads anything itself - your own cloud app does that, and you point it at that one folder. Your originals stay exactly where they are the whole time.
Where do the optimised copies go?

With the default layout, into Pictures/CloudSaver. If you switch to separate folders they go into Pictures/CloudSaver/Photos and Pictures/CloudSaver/Videos instead. In your cloud app, back up only that folder or those folders - nothing else. A small hidden state file lives beside them so CloudSaver can recover its records if the app is reinstalled; it holds names, dates and sizes only, never your pictures.

No. CloudSaver never edits, moves or deletes an original by itself, at any point, for any reason. The only way an original is ever removed is if you open Reclaim space, choose files yourself, and confirm Android’s own deletion dialog. Even then, only files CloudSaver can show reached your cloud are offered.
How much quality is lost, and how is that measured?

On the default Storage saver preset, video is capped at 1080p and keeps roughly 90-95% of the original’s visual quality, and photos are capped at 16 MP where the loss is about 3% and hard to see. Those percentages are estimates for the encoder settings, not measurements of your files. What CloudSaver does measure is size: open Quality explained to see how much your own photos and videos actually shrank. The preset is a ceiling, so a photo already under the limit is left alone.
Are dates, GPS and file names kept?

Yes. Every copy carries the original shooting date, camera details and GPS from the original’s EXIF, and the file date is set to match. That is why the copies appear in your cloud in the same order as your gallery instead of all dated today. The file name keeps the original name with a short unique code added, so two photos with the same name never collide.
How does CloudSaver know a file reached my cloud?

Copies are added to the upload folder a few at a time rather than all at once, and CloudSaver watches how many bytes your cloud app sends. There are three levels of certainty. Strongest: your cloud app removed the copy itself after uploading it - that is direct proof. Next: the copy went out alone and the bytes sent match its size. Weakest: enough time passed with no way to measure. Only the first two can ever offer an original for removal.
What if my cloud app has no duplicate check?

CloudSaver keeps a permanent record of every copy that reached your cloud, matched by content. Once a file is on that list it is never sent again, even if it disappears from the upload folder later - which is exactly what happens when a cloud app tidies up after itself. The record survives reinstalling the app. What CloudSaver cannot control is what your cloud app does with files you add by other means.
How much mobile data does it use?

None of its own. CloudSaver has no internet permission at all, so it physically cannot send anything. All the data is your cloud app uploading the folder, and the daily upload limit is what controls it: by default CloudSaver adds at most 250 MB a day to that folder, so that is the most your cloud app has to upload. Raise or lower it in Settings.
How much phone space does it use?

Two separate limits control this. “Keep this much phone space free” is about your phone: CloudSaver stops working entirely if free space drops below it, so it can never fill your device. “Space CloudSaver may use” is about CloudSaver: it caps the optimised copies waiting to be uploaded, and when it fills, the oldest already-confirmed copies are deleted first. For example, with 1.5 GB free kept and a 1.5 GB app limit, CloudSaver holds at most 1.5 GB of copies and stops if your phone drops under 1.5 GB free.

Home always says which reason applies. It waits for a charger in Charging only mode; it needs battery above 30% (25% on Fast) otherwise; it stops when Battery Saver is on, when the phone is warm, or when the day’s 30 minutes of video work are used - that resets at midnight, and plugging in continues immediately. It also stops if your phone is low on space, and it stops deleting anything if your cloud app looks like it has stopped uploading.
Someone deleted a file from the CloudSaver folder - what now?

If CloudSaver had already confirmed that file reached your cloud, nothing happens: the disappearance is the proof, and the original was never at risk. If it had not been confirmed, CloudSaver simply makes the copy again - up to twice. After the second time it stops and marks the file as removed before upload, because something is clearly deleting copies faster than your cloud can take them, and looping forever would just waste battery.
What about HEIC, RAW, GIF and motion photos?

HEIC photos are converted to JPEG and compressed like any other photo. RAW, GIF, SVG and similar formats are copied byte-for-byte, because compressing them would either fail or destroy what makes them useful. Motion photos, portrait/depth photos and multi-picture files are also copied unchanged, since the extra frames or depth data only survive in the original file. Nothing is ever dropped - every file either gets a smaller copy or an exact one, and Files tells you which.
What happens on uninstall, clear data, or a new phone?

CloudSaver writes a small hidden state file next to your copies and in Documents, and those survive clearing data and reinstalling. On the next launch it reads the newest valid one and restores what it knew, including the record of which files already reached your cloud. Items that come back without proof of upload are marked unverified, and unverified items can never offer an original for removal - so a restore can never cost you a photo. On a brand-new phone, CloudSaver starts fresh unless you restore a backup file yourself.
Which cloud apps work, which do not, and why?

Anything that can back up one folder you choose. Best fit, because they are end-to-end encrypted and do no compression of their own: Ente (recommended), MEGA, Filen and Proton Drive. Also fine: Nextcloud, Immich, OneDrive, or any other app with a custom folder setting. Google Photos and Dropbox cannot work: their mobile apps back up the camera roll and cannot be pointed at one folder, so your originals would upload too.
Cloud storage is full - what happens?

CloudSaver notices that copies are piling up while nothing is being uploaded, tells you once, and stops deleting anything at all until uploads start again. Nothing is lost: your originals are untouched and the copies stay on the phone until its own space limit is reached, after which it simply stops making new ones. Free up room in your cloud or upgrade the plan and it resumes on its own.

No. The internet permission is removed from the app itself, so there is no code path that could send anything anywhere - not analytics, not crash reports, not a file. There are no accounts and no ads. Everything CloudSaver stores stays on the phone: the optimised copies, a local database of what it has done, and the hidden state file. Only your cloud app talks to the internet, and only about the folder you pointed it at.

It is the one screen in CloudSaver that can remove an original, and it only ever removes what you select. Three modes: "Replace with light copy" removes the original and keeps the smaller version in your gallery; "Free up fully" removes the original and keeps nothing locally, so the file lives only in your cloud; "Remove CloudSaver\'s copies only" never touches an original at all. The default is to move files to your gallery\'s trash, where they stay recoverable for 30 days. Android shows its own confirmation dialog every time, because these files belong to your gallery rather than to CloudSaver.
If I remove originals, what will I see in my gallery?

With "Replace with light copy" the photo stays right where it was, at optimised quality, in an album called Light copies. You can still open it, share it and scroll past it - it is simply a smaller file now. With "Free up fully" the photo is gone from the phone and lives only in your cloud, so you open it in your cloud app instead. Both modes leave your cloud exactly as it was.
Can CloudSaver bring a file back from my cloud?

No, and it never will be able to. The app has no internet permission at all, so there is no code path that could download anything. Only your cloud app can fetch a file back. What CloudSaver can do is prefer the trash: files moved there are restorable from your gallery for 30 days, and the Recently reclaimed screen lists them with a Restore button.
How do I free a specific amount of space quickly?

Open Reclaim space and tap one of the target chips - 1 GB, 5 GB or 10 GB. CloudSaver selects eligible files largest-first until it reaches that number, then tells you exactly what it picked. Adjust the selection if you want, tap "Preview result" to see what would happen without anything happening, and check a few files in the compare view first if you want to see the quality for yourself.

By comparing files byte for byte. It first groups files of exactly the same length, since files of different lengths cannot be identical, and only then reads and hashes those - so a large gallery costs very little to check. Files are grouped only when their hashes match, which means they are the same file, not merely similar. CloudSaver keeps the oldest copy and offers the extras; removing an extra is safe even before anything is uploaded, because an identical copy stays on your phone.
Why doesn\'t it find similar photos?

Because that would be a guess. Deciding which of two nearly identical shots is the better one is a judgement about your memory, not a fact about your storage, and a wrong guess deletes the photo you wanted to keep. CloudSaver only acts on things it can prove: hashes, sizes, dates and upload evidence. Your cloud app may offer similar-photo cleanup separately, and that is the right place for it.
Where do reclaimed files go, and can I get them back?

By default into your gallery\'s trash, where Android keeps them for 30 days. The Recently reclaimed screen lists every batch with its files and a Restore button for anything still in the trash. If you chose "Delete permanently" instead, the files are gone and the screen says so plainly. CloudSaver can never re-download anything from your cloud, so the trash is the only local safety net.
What happens to my files if I uninstall CloudSaver?

Your kept light copies stay in Pictures/Light copies and remain in your gallery, because they are ordinary files in an ordinary album. Copies still waiting stay in Pictures/CloudSaver until your cloud app takes them. Temporary work files are removed by Android along with the app. Your cloud is untouched. The app\'s own history survives only in its hidden state file or in a backup you save - Settings has a "Prepare for uninstall" screen that shows all of this and can move the light copies anywhere you like first.
The CloudSaver album disappeared from my gallery - is something wrong?

No. The upload folder is a working folder: once your cloud app has collected the files, it is empty, and galleries hide empty folders. It reappears the next time CloudSaver adds a batch. An empty CloudSaver album is the sign that everything is working, not that something broke.
